note: Meet Egypt, content v3 (10 words). Category Travel & Transport, course level A2.1, unit Meet Egypt.

words.meaning: Customs and ways of doing things that families or a country have kept for a very long time.
situations: Every Ramadan, Egyptian families hang colourful lanterns and eat together after sunset, as their grandparents did.
At weddings in Upper Egypt, people still dance with sticks, just like hundreds of years ago.
gaps: Hanging lanterns in Ramadan is one of Egypt's oldest ______.
Every family has its own holiday ______.
Young people should learn about their country's ______.
hints: Old customs passed from parents to children.

commonMistakes.sentence: We have a tradition to eat fish on Sham El-Nessim.
commonMistakes.correction: We have a tradition of eating fish on Sham El-Nessim.

words.meaning: Visiting famous and interesting places as a tourist.
situations: On their first day in Cairo, the tourists visited the Pyramids, the Egyptian Museum and Khan El-Khalili.
We spent the morning taking photos of old mosques and temples in Luxor.
gaps: We spent the whole day ______ in Cairo.
Luxor is perfect for ______ — there are temples everywhere.
After a week of ______, we relaxed on the beach.
hints: Visiting famous places as a tourist.

words.meaning: The quality of happily giving money, food, time or help to others.
situations: The old shop owner gave free bread to every poor family in the street during Ramadan.
When I lost my wallet, a stranger paid for my train ticket and refused to take the money back.
gaps: Thank you for your ______ — the donation will help many families.
Egyptians are known for their ______ during Ramadan.
Her ______ surprised everyone; she gave away half her salary.

commonMistakes.sentence: He is famous for his generous.
commonMistakes.correction: He is famous for his generosity.
commonMistakes.why: 'Generous' is the adjective; the noun is 'generosity'.

words.meaning: The typical style of cooking and the dishes of a country or region.
situations: Koshari, molokhia and ful are famous dishes from Egypt.
The restaurant serves sushi and ramen cooked the traditional way in Japan.
gaps: Egyptian ______ is famous for dishes like koshari and molokhia.
I love trying the local ______ when I travel.
This hotel restaurant serves Italian ______.
hints: A country's style of cooking and its dishes.

commonMistakes.correction: I love Egyptian cuisine / Egyptian food.
commonMistakes.why: 'Cuisine' already means food style — don't add 'food'.

words.meaning: Being friendly and welcoming to guests and visitors, and taking good care of them.
situations: When we visited a village near Aswan, a family invited us in, made us tea and wouldn't let us leave without lunch.
The hotel staff greeted us with cold juice and helped us with our bags.
gaps: Egyptian ______ is famous — people always invite you for tea.
Thank you for your warm ______ during our stay.
He works in the ______ industry, in hotels and restaurants.

commonMistakes.sentence: They showed us a great hospitable.
commonMistakes.why: 'Hospitable' is the adjective; the noun is 'hospitality'.

words.meaning: Great comfort and expensive, beautiful things that you enjoy but don't really need.
situations: The Nile cruise had a private pool, gold taps and a chef who cooked anything we wanted.
The hotel room in Sharm had a private beach, a huge bed and free champagne.
gaps: We stayed in a ______ hotel with a private beach.
A Nile cruise is a real ______.
They live a life of ______ with expensive cars and big houses.

commonMistakes.correction: The hotel was very luxurious. / It was a luxury hotel.

words.meaning: The whole way of life of a group of people — their art, music, beliefs, language and habits.
situations: Egypt's music, food, language and religion make life there very different from life in Japan.
When she moved to Cairo, Anna learned Arabic, cooked local food and listened to Umm Kulthum.
gaps: Egyptian ______ is a mix of African, Arab and Mediterranean influences.
Travelling helps you learn about other ______s.
Music is a big part of our ______.
hints: A people's whole way of life: art, food, beliefs.

commonMistakes.sentence: I want to learn the culture of Egypt people.
commonMistakes.correction: I want to learn about Egyptian culture.

words.meaning: The ability to find things funny and to make other people laugh.
situations: Even when the bus broke down in the desert, our Egyptian guide made jokes and had everyone laughing.
My grandmother laughs at everything and always knows a joke that makes us smile.
gaps: Egyptians are famous for their great ______ — they joke about everything.
He has no ______; he never laughs at my jokes.
A good ______ helps you in difficult times.
hints: The ability to laugh and make others laugh.
Three words: 'sense of' + a word for funniness.

commonMistakes.sentence: She has a good humor sense.
commonMistakes.correction: She has a good sense of humor.
commonMistakes.why: The fixed phrase is 'sense of humor' (UK: humour).

words.meaning: The large sea between southern Europe, northern Africa and western Asia, on Egypt's north coast.
situations: From Alexandria, you can look north across the water towards Greece and Italy.
In summer, many Egyptian families go to the north coast to swim in the blue water.
gaps: Alexandria is on the coast of the ______.
Egypt has beaches on both the Red Sea and the ______.
Greece, Italy and Egypt all have coasts on the ______.
hints: The big sea north of Egypt.

commonMistakes.sentence: Alexandria is on the Mediterranean ocean.
commonMistakes.correction: Alexandria is on the Mediterranean Sea.
commonMistakes.why: It's a sea, not an ocean.

words.meaning: Cities built next to the sea or ocean.
situations: Alexandria, Port Said and Marsa Matrouh all have beaches and ports right in the city.
In summer, many Cairo families travel north to big towns by the sea to escape the heat.
gaps: Alexandria and Port Said are famous ______ in Egypt.
Many ______ have busy ports and fresh fish markets.
Rising sea levels are a danger for ______.
